newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The country's GDP growth rate will go upto 5.7 percent at the end of the current 1996-97 fiscal year (July-June), the highest in last ten years.
Four councillors of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), including its vice chairman, resigned on Monday, paving the way for reorganisation of the DSE board.
The cabinet on Monday approved the national policy on HIV/AIDS and STD related diseases.

At least 25 students were injured in a gunfight between the pro-government student activists and student front of the fundamentalist Jmaat e Islami party at the Chittagong University campus area on Tuesday.
Nearly 100 foreign entrepreneurs have registered themselves with the Board of Investment (BOI) during the last nine months for investment about Taka 1,754 crore in Bangladesh.
Two people were killed and 10 others injured when a nor-wester lashed Dhaka city on Monday.
Commerce and Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed on Monday said Bangladesh had become the market of others, specially of India, since 1994 when its drastically reduced import tariff.
Dhaka Stock Exchange chairman, Imtiyaz Husain, said on Monday that the bourse would go for early election of its council. REUTER
